result:
I wrote lesson 1, "Context and memory in an agent": a 60-minute lesson on objective O3, with a short quiz ready for you.

I estimate about 7,500 words, roughly 0.83 of the 9,000 a 60-minute lesson targets. It runs on the makerspace assistant throughout, and the time costs are priced out.

What it covers:
- **Context window:** what fills it, what a token is, and why it limits both accuracy and cost.
- **Between steps:** the model keeps nothing, and the program resends the whole message list on every call. A five-call 3D-printer request reads 18,830 input tokens. The lesson proves why longer runs cost more than proportionally.
- **Trimming a full window:** clearing old tool results, compaction and helper agents, each with a worked example.
- **Between sessions:** notes and the memory tool. A note never decides whether a student may use a machine. The training record is read through a tool on each request.
- **Retrieval:** pasting a manual costs about 17 times more than retrieving five chunks. It also covers keyword search, cosine similarity, and Anthropic's published retrieval-failure figures.
- **Practice:** a worked request end to end, then several short exercises to compute and classify.

The lesson went through two content reviews, a preference review, a reference check and a consistency edit. The reference check found no missing or contradicted sources.

The 0.75-words-per-token rule, the $3 and $15 per million token prices, and the cosine and keyword-weighting formulas are not from the cited sources. The lesson labels each of them as a rule of thumb, an illustration or a standard formula.

Quiz 0002 has five items on this objective, and I did not read its answers into this message. A cheat sheet with the placement rules and token arithmetic is saved too, and I updated your notes.

Questions on any part are welcome in the chat. Ask for the quiz whenever you want to check what stuck.
